title: 1974 AHSME Problem 23
statement: In the adjoining figure \(TP\) and \(T'Q\) are parallel tangents to a circle of radius \(r,\) with \(T\) and \(T'\) the points of tangency. \(PT''Q\) is a third tangent with \(T''\) as point of tangency. If \(TP=4\) and \(T'Q=9\) then \(r\) is

answerChoices.label: E
answerChoices.text: not determinable from the given information

solutions.text:
The radii to the tangency points make congruent right triangles from each external point, so \(OP\) and \(OQ\) bisect the two tangent angles. Because the other two tangents are parallel, these half-angles add to \(90^\circ;\) hence \(\angle POQ=90^\circ.\)

Thus \(OT''=r\) is the altitude to the hypotenuse \(PQ.\) Equal tangent segments give \(PT''=PT=4\) and \(QT''=QT'=9.\) The altitude theorem yields \[ r^2=(PT'')(QT'')=4\cdot9=36, \] so \(r=6.\)

Therefore, the correct answer is B.
hints: The center lies on each angle bisector formed by two tangents from the same external point
Show that \(\angle POQ=90^\circ\) and use the altitude-to-hypotenuse theorem at \(T''\)
